key_insight: The paper uses reinforcement learning to adaptively choose neighborhood size in recovery optimization, finding high-quality feasible log-truck schedules faster than fixed search strategies.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical decision-support method for dispatchers to quickly replan transportation operations after disruptions while balancing schedule stability and operating cost.
method: Formulate recovery as a sequence of MILPs constrained by an _1 deviation bound k from the baseline plan.
Compute the minimum feasible deviation k_min exactly to anchor the search at the most stable feasible point.
Train a REINFORCE policy to select successive k values from solver feedback and build a Pareto front of recovery options.
evidence_signal: On weekly real-world instances from a Canadian forestry partner, the method produced richer Pareto fronts with fewer solver calls than fixed-grid and dichotomic baselines across all disruption categories.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable solver feedback and trained policy behavior, so performance may vary when disruption patterns or instance structure differ from the training and evaluation data.
paper_title: Learning to recover: Adaptive local branching with reinforcement learning for log-truck routing and scheduling under disruptions
